# esp-atlas

> A community-maintained, datasheet-verified knowledge base for the entire ESP32
> family — SoCs, modules, dev boards, AND the firmware that runs on them (Cardputer,
> M5Stack, Flipper-devboard, and pentest/RF tools like Marauder, Bruce, Ghost ESP,
> Meshcore). Stored as plain markdown with YAML frontmatter; every hard spec cites an
> official source — if it isn't verified, it isn't stated. Each firmware page is a
> flash guide: which board it runs on, what it does, and how to flash it. Queryable
> via search/wizard and a JSON API, and every page also serves a clean markdown view
> for LLMs and agents (append `?format=md`).

esp-atlas exists because most ESP32 guides are one person's blog, frozen at publish
date, with unverified specs and no way to query them. This repo is the opposite:
open data, git-versioned, source-cited, and machine-queryable. Contributions —
human or agent — follow search-before-add, copy-template, fill-with-citations,
self-validate, then PR.

## Site

- [esp-atlas.com](https://esp-atlas.com): the live site — wizard and search on `/`,
  one page per part at `/parts/<id>` (SoCs, modules, boards), side-by-side `/compare`.
- Firmware catalog: one page per firmware at `/firmware/<id>` — a flash guide with the
  boards it runs on, its capabilities, and cited popularity. Browse all at `/firmware`.
  Append `?format=md` to any page for a token-efficient markdown view built for agents.
- [API](https://esp-atlas.com/api/docs): `GET /api/parts`, `GET /api/parts/{id}`,
  `GET /api/search?q=&soc=&brand=&type=`, `GET /api/facets`, `POST /api/wizard` — the same
  records as JSON, every spec with its source.
- [sitemap.xml](https://esp-atlas.com/sitemap.xml): every part page, with the date
  its sources were last verified.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): project overview, data layout, status.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): contributor guide for AI coding agents — data model, hard
  rules, required workflow.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): human contribution guide (same rules as AGENTS.md).
- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): project vision, data model, interface layers, phasing.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): retrieval design — repo-as-database, index build,
  grounded chat layer.
- [INTERFACE-SPEC.md](INTERFACE-SPEC.md): API/CLI/site contracts and milestones.

## Data

- [schema/](schema/): JSON Schema contracts (`soc.schema.json`, `module.schema.json`,
  `board.schema.json`) — the authoritative field list for every record.
- [data/](data/): the dataset itself — `socs/`, `modules/`, `boards/`, `brands/`,
  `companions/`, `firmware/`, `recipes/` — one markdown file per record, YAML
  frontmatter + prose, every spec source-cited.
- [templates/](templates/): blank soc/module/board templates to copy when adding a
  new record — every field commented with what it is and its source requirement.

## Tools

- `esp-atlas search "<query>"` (CLI) / `GET /search?q=` (API): search the dataset
  before adding a record, to avoid duplicates.
- `esp-atlas validate <file>` (CLI) / `POST /validate` (API): validate a record's
  frontmatter against schema + source-or-omit + inheritance rules before opening a PR.
- `python3 scripts/validate.py`: the same validation, run over the whole dataset —
  the CI gate.

## Optional

- [skills/esp-atlas/SKILL.md](skills/esp-atlas/SKILL.md): the contributor workflow as
